gemini.performance_metric: net sales grew to $7,095 million and net income to $340 million in fiscal 2017
gemini.rationale: The evidence slice notes that the company deliberately kept the Avintiv acquisition as a separate segment 'in order to maintain management continuity and limit business integration risk,' avoiding process/organization fracture. There is no documented evidence of product/process disruption, with only minor plant shutdown impairments and standard integration costs reported.

grok.performance_metric: net sales $4.9–7.1bn, NI $86–340M FY15–17; no GW impairment
grok.rationale: The slice documents no product/process interface disruption: only minor $2–3M PP&E impairment charges tied to plant shutdowns in FY2015–16, with zero goodwill or indefinite-lived intangible impairments and rising operating income ($408M to $732M). On process/organization, the Company deliberately kept Avintiv as a segment-level carve-out ‘to maintain management continuity and limit business integration risk,’ incurred routine $10M business-integration/restructuring costs, and had not yet folded AEP into its internal-control framework by FY2017 year-end—none of which is framed as a realized fracture of operations against organization. Growth was driven by further retained acquisitions (Avintiv, AEP) and a rename to Berry Global, with no documented archetype or business-model incoherence.

openai.performance_metric: net income increased from $86 million in fiscal 2015 to $340 million in fiscal 2017
openai.rationale: No realized product/process incoherence is documented; the filings instead report rising operating income and no goodwill or indefinite-lived intangible impairment in fiscal 2015 or 2016. For the process/organization interface, Berry preserved Avintiv management to limit integration risk and incurred $10 million of integration costs, while AEP/Adchem controls had not yet been evaluated by fiscal 2017; these facts document cautious or incomplete integration, but not an organizational fracture or breakdown.
